rules.title: Dart badCertificateCallback accepts every certificate
rules.why: A `badCertificateCallback` that returns `true` turns off TLS server checks for Dart's HttpClient, and for Dio or package:http clients built on it. Anyone on the same network can impersonate your server and read or change the traffic.
rules.fix: Delete the callback, or return `false` from it. For a local test server, trust its certificate in a debug-only `SecurityContext` instead. If you need pinning, use `SecurityContext(withTrustedRoots: false)` with your CA's certificate, which keeps the normal checks.
rules.verify: Send the app's traffic through a proxy whose CA the phone doesn't trust and confirm every request fails with a HandshakeException.

rules.title: Token or password stored in shared_preferences
rules.why: shared_preferences writes a plain XML file on Android and a UserDefaults plist on iOS. Both are copied into backups and are readable by anyone with access to the device's files, so a long-lived token there can be lifted and replayed.
rules.fix: Keep short-lived tokens in memory. Store long-lived tokens and credentials with `flutter_secure_storage`, which uses the Android Keystore and the iOS Keychain, and set `IOSOptions(accessibility: KeychainAccessibility.first_unlock_this_device)` or stricter. Leave only non-secret settings in shared_preferences.
rules.verify: Sign in on an emulator, then run `adb shell run-as <package> cat shared_prefs/FlutterSharedPreferences.xml` and confirm no token or password appears.

rules.title: Dio logger prints headers or bodies in release builds
rules.why: PrettyDioLogger, and a LogInterceptor with a custom `logPrint` (or on dio 4), print every request with `print`, which reaches logcat and the device console in release builds. The `Authorization` header and login responses end up in logs and bug reports.
rules.fix: Add logging interceptors only under `if (kDebugMode)`, and redact the `Authorization` and cookie headers in any logger that stays.
rules.verify: Install a release build, sign in, and watch `adb logcat` or Console.app: no request headers, tokens, or response bodies should appear.

rules.title: Flutter web view can read local files or load mixed content
rules.why: With file-origin access on, a page loaded from a file can read other local files, such as the app's databases, and send them anywhere. Allowing mixed content lets an HTTPS page pull scripts over plain HTTP that anyone on the network can replace.
rules.fix: Remove these flutter_inappwebview settings. Serve bundled HTML through `webViewAssetLoader` over `https://appassets.androidplatform.net` instead of `file://` URLs.
rules.verify: Search for `allowFileAccessFromFileURLs`, `allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs`, `allowFileAccess: true`, and `MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW`; none should remain.

fix_code.code:
InAppWebView(
  initialSettings: InAppWebViewSettings(
    allowFileAccess: false,
    allowFileAccessFromFileURLs: false,
    allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs: false,
    mixedContentMode: MixedContentMode.MIXED_CONTENT_NEVER_ALLOW,
    webViewAssetLoader: WebViewAssetLoader(
      pathHandlers: [AssetsPathHandler(path: '/assets/')],
    ),
  ),
  initialUrlRequest: URLRequest(
    url: WebUri('https://appassets.androidplatform.net/assets/flutter_assets/web/index.html'),
  ),
)

rules.title: Flutter web view accepts any server certificate
rules.why: A trust handler that answers PROCEED without checking the certificate turns off TLS for the web view. Anyone on the same network can serve their own page with a self-signed certificate and read or change what the user sees and types.
rules.fix: Delete the handler so the platform validates the chain, or return `CANCEL` unless your own pin check on the server certificate passes.
rules.verify: Route the device through a proxy whose CA it doesn't trust; the web view should refuse to load the page.

rules.title: Flutter web view debugging is on in release
rules.why: With web contents debugging or `isInspectable` on, anyone holding the device can attach Chrome DevTools or Safari's Web Inspector, read cookies and tokens from the page, and run their own script in it.
rules.fix: Pass `kDebugMode` instead of `true`, so debugging is on only in debug builds.
rules.verify: Install a release build and open `chrome://inspect` (or Safari's Develop menu); the app's web view should not be listed.

rules.title: Flutter biometric check only returns a boolean
rules.why: local_auth's `authenticate()` returns true or false and unlocks nothing. On a rooted or jailbroken device a hook makes it return true, and since no key needed the biometric, the protected data opens anyway.
rules.fix: Keep the secret under a key that only biometric authentication unlocks, with `biometric_storage` or a platform channel to a Keystore key with a CryptoObject or a Keychain item with `SecAccessControl`. Don't gate on the boolean.
rules.verify: Hook `authenticate` to return true with Frida (`frida -U -f <app>`); the protected data should still stay locked because no key was released.

rules.title: Flutter release build is not obfuscated
rules.why: Without `--obfuscate`, the compiled Dart code keeps its class and function names, so tools such as blutter map the app's logic, including its integrity and root checks, in minutes.
rules.fix: Add `--obfuscate --split-debug-info=build/symbols` to every release `flutter build` command, and keep the symbol files to decode crash reports.
rules.verify: Run `strings` on `libapp.so` from the release APK and confirm your own class names, such as your login screen's, no longer appear.

fix_code.code:
- run: flutter build appbundle --release --obfuscate --split-debug-info=build/symbols
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4   # keep symbols to decode crashes
  with:
    name: dart-symbols
    path: build/symbols
